subChunks.title: ROWS BETWEEN and RANGE BETWEEN
subChunks.hookHtml: Window frames control exactly which rows participate in each window function computation. Understanding frames is what separates novice window function users from experts.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Default frame

When you write ORDER BY col in OVER, the default frame is RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW — a growing window from the first row to the current row.

ROWS BETWEEN

-- 3-row moving average:
SELECT name, xp,
  AVG(xp) OVER (
    ORDER BY id
    ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING
  ) AS moving_avg
FROM apprentices;

-- Running total from start to current:
SELECT name, xp,
  SUM(xp) OVER (
    ORDER BY id
    ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
  ) AS cumulative_xp
FROM apprentices;

RANGE BETWEEN vs ROWS BETWEEN

  • ROWS — physical row count (1 PRECEDING = exactly 1 row back)
  • RANGE — logical value range (1 PRECEDING on a date column = 1 unit before the current value — all rows with that date)

Frame boundaries

  • UNBOUNDED PRECEDING — the first row in the partition
  • n PRECEDING — n rows/units before current row
  • CURRENT ROW — the current row
  • n FOLLOWING — n rows/units after current row
  • UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING — the last row in the partition

storyBeats.text: The XP chart needs a 3-week moving average — not a running total, not a rank, but a sliding window of three consecutive values.

storyBeats.speaker: Cipher the Archivist
storyBeats.text: The frame clause tells the window where to look. UNBOUNDED PRECEDING to CURRENT ROW is the default for running totals. ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING is a 3-row sliding window. ROWS counts physical rows; RANGE counts by value. Choose deliberately.

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
🪄 Moving average

Return name, xp, and a 3-row moving average (current row + 1 preceding + 1 following) of xp ordered by id, aliased as moving_avg.
subChunks.guidedPracticeStarterCode:
SELECT name, xp,
  AVG(xp) OVER (
    ORDER BY id
    ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING
  ) AS moving_avg
FROM apprentices
ORDER BY id;

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain the difference between ROWS BETWEEN and RANGE BETWEEN, and describe what UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW means.

questions.prompt: What does `ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` specify?
options: The frame includes all rows from the start of the partition up to and including the current row — the standard running total frame
The frame includes the current row only
The frame includes all rows in the partition
The frame includes 1 row before and 1 row after the current row
questions.answer: The frame includes all rows from the start of the partition up to and including the current row — the standard running total frame
questions.explanation: UNBOUNDED PRECEDING = first row of partition. CURRENT ROW = the row being computed. Together they define a growing window — each row sees all rows up to itself, which is the running total pattern.

questions.prompt: `ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` — how many rows does the frame include for the 3rd row?
options: All rows from row 1 to row 3 plus 2 rows after
questions.explanation: 2 PRECEDING means 2 rows back. For row 3: row 1 (2 back), row 2 (1 back), row 3 (current). That is 3 rows. For row 1 (the first), there are no preceding rows — the frame collapses to just row 1.

questions.prompt: When would you use `ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING`?
options: When you want FIRST_VALUE or LAST_VALUE to always return the true first/last row of the entire partition
For comparing each row to the previous row with LAG
questions.answer: When you want FIRST_VALUE or LAST_VALUE to always return the true first/last row of the entire partition
questions.explanation: The default frame ends at CURRENT ROW, so LAST_VALUE only returns the current row's value. UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING extends the frame to the partition end, making LAST_VALUE return the true last value in the partition.

questions.prompt: RANGE BETWEEN 7 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW on a DATE column — what does '7 PRECEDING' mean?
options: All rows whose date value is within 7 days before the current row's date
Exactly 7 rows before the current row in physical order
The row exactly 7 positions earlier in the ORDER BY sequence
questions.answer: All rows whose date value is within 7 days before the current row's date
questions.explanation: RANGE operates on value ranges, not physical row offsets. For a DATE column, RANGE 7 PRECEDING means: include all rows whose date is <= current_date AND >= current_date - 7. This is how you compute a true 7-day rolling window even when some days have multiple rows or missing dates.
